messages:
Anna M: Heads-up — I'm drafting controls for per-customer slice rollouts on Dedicated. Need opinions on isolation vs traffic flexibility. Proposal: route-level traffic splits (per-route canaries) + a global safety cap per customer. Thoughts?

Mike R: +1 to route-level. Quick Q: do we keep session stickiness for chat flows or route by request hash?

Anna M: For chat we should sticky at session-id to avoid mid-conversation model jumps. For stateless requests (embeddings/batch) use consistent hashing.

Jess K: Dashboard requirement: show per-slice p50/p95 latency, error-rate (4xx vs 5xx), throughput, and token-cost delta vs control. Ops needs to see the cost impact alongside perf.

Lex: Telemetry note — emit tags: customer_id, slice_id, rollout_id, route, split_pct. Also include a sampled request_id for trace linking.

Sam T: On quotas: Dedicated customers have reserved capacity but canary traffic must not exceed a safety envelope. We need both a per-customer soft cap (percent of reserved) and a hard cluster throttle.

Anna M: Agreed. Draft guard policy (example):
```yaml
rollout_id: r-2026-03-09-03
customer: acme-corp
slices:
  - id: slice-A
    routes: ["/chat", "/tools/call"]
    traffic_split: 0.03 # 3%
guards:
  max_pct_of_customer_reservation: 0.10 # 10% of reserved GPU pool
  cpu_threshold: 0.72 # abort if slice CPU > 72% for 2m
  error_rate_threshold: 0.02 # abort if p95 5xx > 2%
fallback:
  - model: stable-v1
    action: immediate-fallback
```

Mike R: Small nit: split the error guard into 4xx vs 5xx — 4xx can be rate/validation; 5xx is platform regression. Also consider p50 recovery window before aborting.

Jess K: UX: console should surface a quick 'health summary' for the slice: green/yellow/red with the key signals and a sparkline for latency and error rate. Also a small diff view comparing sampled responses between canary and control (quality regression snapshots).

Lex: For observability presets, add two templates: latency-sensitive (tight latency and error thresholds) and quality-sensitive (allow higher latency but stricter quality checks). These appear as dropdowns when creating rollouts.

Anna M: Good. Also want a lightweight A/B mode where we record but do not bill canary traffic for cost analysis, plus a 'shadow' option that sends copies of traffic for scoring only.

Sam T: Implementation question: quota enforcement should be in the router layer, not just admission. Router must respect both per-customer split and cluster headroom and expose metrics when it rejects/defers a canary request.

DeployBot: deploy started for r-2026-03-09-03 -> slice-A canary (3%): host: prod-router-12, commit: 7f4b3c9

Mike R: Nice — when the deploy completes can the router emit a 'slice_active' event with current split and effective capacity? That helps dashboards show expected vs actual.

Jess K: We'll add expected_vs_actual traffic card. Also add a small sampled-response panel (5 requests/min) with side-by-side tokens/cost/llm_output diff.

Anna M: I'll update the rollout API spec and console mocks. Plan: enforce guards server-side, router emits metrics, console shows preset pickers + diff, and HQ alerting triggers on guard aborts.

Lex: One more: rollouts API should accept an optional 'safety_override' flag that only SRE+Platform can set for emergency fast-forwarding. Audit logs mandatory.

Sam T: LGTM. I'll pair with Anna tomorrow to finalize quota checks and a short integration test for router-enforced caps.

Anna M: Thanks all. I'll push the API PR and mock screenshots later today. :rocket:
